title: Bind Core2 legacy late wait to LVGL and add a partial SPI transaction-done IRQ model

firmware.name: UIFlow_Core2 v1.15.4
firmware.reason: The virtual device reached the LVGL flush wait and observed the flush callback, but not the SPI completion callback or lv_disp_flush_ready.

execution.environment: macOS 25.5.0 arm64, Python 3.13.15, retained Core2 QEMU tree

checks.name: bin_bound_lvgl_mapping
checks.detail: 0x40100010 is bound to lv_refr_vdb_flush; 0x40174884 is the display flush completion callback and 0x402605ec is lv_disp_flush_ready.

checks.name: late_state_object_binding
checks.detail: A2 is lv_disp_buf_t with two valid buffers and flushing=1; A10 is the display driver with flush_cb=0x40174758 and wait_cb=null.

checks.name: display_flush_callback
checks.detail: The flush callback was observed once in the WDT-off trace before and after the SPI IRQ model change.

checks.name: display_completion_callback
checks.detail: Neither the completion callback nor lv_disp_flush_ready was observed in the 50-second WDT-off windows.

checks.name: spi_transaction_done_irq_level
checks.detail: TRANS_DONE and TRANS_INTEN are stateful and produce IRQ level 1, but the guest completion path still does not run.

checks.name: normal_wdt_boot
checks.detail: TG0 stage-1 reset occurred at about 15.9157 seconds; TG1 remained live, serial had no REPL and the frame remained a 302-byte black image.

checks.name: platform_contracts
checks.detail: All 544 platform tests and the Core2 documentation contract passed.

checks.name: generated_registries
checks.detail: Runtime coverage, peripheral catalog, QEMU profiles and project snapshot checks passed.

checks.name: patch_replay
checks.detail: The 0042 patch passed reverse apply checking in the matching retained QEMU tree.

checks.name: ci
checks.detail: Product CI run 40254086653 passed both jobs on result commit f206175.

checks.name: full_peripheral_matrix
checks.detail: This diagnostic did not rerun the full 67-case matrix.

notes: This is virtual-device and BIN-bound static evidence, not hardware validation.
The flush callback is not equivalent to a completed frame.
An IRQ level of 1 does not prove guest interrupt delivery, ISR execution or queue completion.
No restricted firmware or device artifacts were added.
